nodes.summary: For sets $S$ and $T$ of bitstrings, their concatenation is the set of all bitstrings $uv$ with $u \in S$ and $v \in T$.
nodes.title: Concatenation of bitstring languages

nodes.summary: A list of natural-number tokens is evaluated from left to right on a given stack of languages of bitstrings. Token $0$ pushes the empty language, token $1$ pushes the language containing only the empty bitstring, and tokens $2$ and $3$ push the languages containing only the one-letter bitstring false, respectively true. Token $4$ pops the top language $S$ and the language $T$ below it and pushes the concatenation…
nodes.title: Evaluation of postfix regular expressions with squaring

nodes.summary: The universality problem for postfix regular expressions with squaring belongs to $\mathsf{EXPSPACE}$, and every decision problem in $\mathsf{EXPSPACE}$ reduces to it by a polynomial-time many-one reduction. Here the universality problem accepts a bitstring exactly when it decodes to a list of natural-number tokens whose postfix evaluation, started on the empty stack, returns the set of all bitstrings.
nodes.title: Regular expressions with squaring: universality is EXPSPACE-complete

nodes.summary: This is the decision problem that accepts a bitstring $x$ exactly when $x$ decodes, under the canonical bitstring encoding of lists of natural numbers, to a token list whose evaluation as a postfix regular expression with squaring, started on the empty stack, succeeds and returns the set of all bitstrings. A bitstring that does not decode to a list of natural numbers is rejected.
nodes.title: Universality of postfix regular expressions with squaring

nodes.summary: For a set $S$ of bitstrings, its Kleene star is the set of all concatenations $u_1 u_2 \cdots u_k$, for $k \ge 0$, of bitstrings $u_1, \dots, u_k \in S$; the empty concatenation ($k = 0$) is the empty bitstring.
nodes.title: Kleene star of a bitstring language

can_prove.label: ready to prove
can_prove.meaning: Statement is in Lean and nothing it needs is blocked, so the proof can start.

can_state.label: ready to state
can_state.meaning: Everything its statement uses is in Lean, so the statement can be written in Lean.

conditional.label: conditionally proved
conditional.meaning: Proof compiles, but rests on an open statement without a recorded Lean proof.

fully_proved.label: fully proved
fully_proved.meaning: Proved, and every prerequisite is fully proved too.

inventory_checked.label: inventory checked
inventory_checked.meaning: Module inventory checked in full; it records inspection, not a mathematical proof.

inventory_pending.label: inventory pending
inventory_pending.meaning: Module inventory not yet checked in full; it records inspection, not a mathematical proof.

not_ready.label: not ready
not_ready.meaning: Needs more blueprint work before it can be attempted.

proved.label: proved
proved.meaning: Proof compiles, but something it rests on is not finished.

stated.label: statement formalized
stated.meaning: Statement is in Lean; the proof is not.
